nodes.speaker: Nikias
nodes.text: Welcome to Piraeus, captain. The merchant house of Kephalos has need of your services.

nodes.speaker: Nikias
nodes.text: Ah, captain! How fares the commission? Have you secured the Attic pottery and the Tyrian purple?

choices.text: I am still working on it.

nodes.speaker: Nikias
nodes.text: Captain! You have done the house of Kephalos a great service. The Tyrian purple is magnificent -- the priests of Athena will be most pleased. Your reputation in Athens grows.

nodes.speaker: Nikias
nodes.text: We need fine Attic pottery delivered to the Phoenician merchants at Tyre, and in return, you must bring back their famous purple dye. The festival of Athena approaches and the priests require new vestments.

effects.title: The Tyrian Commission
effects.text: The merchant Nikias of Athens has tasked me with delivering Attic pottery to Tyre and returning with Tyrian purple dye for the festival of Athena.

nodes.speaker: Nikias
nodes.text: Excellent. First, purchase Attic pottery here at Piraeus -- at least five crates. Deliver them to Tyre, then buy the purple dye and bring it back. May Poseidon grant you fair winds.

nodes.speaker: Nikias
nodes.text: A cautious captain lives longer, I suppose. Return if you change your mind.

nodes.speaker: Nikias
nodes.text: The Phoenicians of Tyre produce the finest purple dye in all the Mediterranean -- extracted from the murex snail. It is worth more than silver by weight. We trade our pottery for their dye.

choices.text: Tell me more about Tyrian purple.

nodes.speaker: Nikias
nodes.text: Each murex yields but a single drop. It takes ten thousand shells to dye one garment. The Phoenicians have guarded this secret for centuries. Pliny himself wrote of its magnificence.

choices.text: Fascinating. I will seek it out.

nodes.speaker: Nikias
nodes.text: Remember -- buy Attic pottery here at Piraeus, deliver it to Tyre, purchase their purple dye, and return it to me. The festival cannot wait forever.

nodes.speaker: Nikias
nodes.text: Indeed it was. You are always welcome at the house of Kephalos, captain. Perhaps we shall have more work for you in the future.
